title: Mortgage Advisor Salary: Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Pay Under the Real Estate Award

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied to a mortgage advisor salary?

faqs.q: What is the annual salary for a Level 2 mortgage advisor including super?
faqs.a: A full-time Level 2 mortgage advisor working 38 hours per week earns $29.45 × 38 × 52 = $58,173.20 per year. bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Mortgage Advisor Salary

If you're working as a mortgage advisor or considering the role, knowing how your hourly rate translates into annual, fortnightly, and take-home pay is essential. Mortgage advisors in Australia are typically covered by the **Real Estate Industry Award 2020** (MA000106), which sets minimum wages, penalty rates, and casual loadings. This guide explains how to convert an hourly rate into annual salary, using the award rates from 1 July 2026, and distinguishes between the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, and superannuation.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours per Week × 52

The standard calculation for annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a full-time week of **38 ordinary hours**, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. For part-time employees, use the agreed weekly hours. This formula assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no salary sacrifice. It's an estimate, not a binding determination.

For example, a full-time mortgage advisor at **Level 2 (Representative Level)** earns $29.45 per hour. Their annual salary is:

$29.45 × 38 × 52 = **$58,173.20**

A fortnightly pay (every two weeks) would be $29.45 × 38 × 2 = **$2,238.20** before tax and super.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the **National Minimum Wage** is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, most mortgage advisors are covered by the Real Estate Industry Award, which has higher minimum rates. The award classifies employees into four levels:

- **Level 1 (Associate)** – first 12 months: $26.59/hr
- **Level 1 (Associate)** – after 12 months: $28.00/hr
- **Level 2 (Representative)** – typical for mortgage advisors: **$29.45/hr**
- **Level 3 (Supervisory)**: $32.39/hr
- **Level 4 (In-Charge)**: $33.88/hr

These rates apply from the first full pay period on or after 1 July 2026. Always check the [pay guides](/blog) for your specific classification.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees receive a **25% loading** on top of the minimum hourly rate. For a Level 2 mortgage advisor, the casual rate is $29.45 × 1.25 = **$36.81 per hour**. This loading is paid for all ordinary hours and replaces entitlements like annual leave and sick leave. When calculating annual pay for a casual, use the loaded rate in the same formula: $36.81 × 38 × 52 = **$72,736.56**.

**Superannuation** is paid on top of ordinary earnings at **12%** (the super guarantee rate for 2026-27). The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year. For a full-time Level 2 mortgage advisor, super adds $58,173.20 × 0.12 = **$6,980.78** per year. This is an employer contribution and does not reduce your take-home pay.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Using the 2026-27 resident tax rates:
- Nil tax on first $18,200
- 15% on income between $18,201 and $45,000
- 30% on income between $45,001 and $135,000
- 37% on income between $135,001 and $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the **Medicare levy** of 2% (using the 2025-26 single reduction thresholds as 2026-27 thresholds were not confirmed).

For a $58,173 annual salary:
- Tax on $58,173: ($45,000 - $18,200) × 0.15 + ($58,173 - $45,000) × 0.30 = $4,020 + $3,951.90 = **$7,971.90**
- Medicare levy: $58,173 × 0.02 = **$1,163.46**
- Total tax and Medicare: **$9,135.36**
- Estimated take-home: **$49,037.84** per year (before any HELP or surcharges)

Use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to estimate your own figures.

### Comparing with Average Earnings

The **Australian Bureau of Statistics** (ABS) reports Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time as $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). That equates to an annual salary of about $108,352. A mortgage advisor at Level 2 ($58,173) is below this average, but experienced advisors or those on higher classifications (Level 3 or 4) may earn more. The all-employees average (including part-time) is $1,579.20 per week ($82,118 annually).

### Key Takeaways

- Mortgage advisor salary under the Real Estate Industry Award starts at $26.59/hr for Level 1 and rises to $33.88/hr for Level 4.
- Full-time annual pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52. Fortnightly = hourly × 38 × 2.
- Casual loading adds 25% to the base rate.
- Super is 12% paid on top, not deducted from your pay.
- Tax and Medicare reduce gross pay; use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) estimator for a personalised calculation.

Always refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) and the award for your exact classification and any applicable allowances or penalty rates.
